Last month, OpenAI teased a hardware product named Codex. A month later, the company has officially unveiled the result of its collaboration with Work Louder: a Codex Micro keyboard priced at US$230.

Below is the product introduction:

The keyboard comes in two versions: Clicky (青軸) and Silent.

The official website states: "Each Agent key uses RGB lighting to display the real-time status of Codex, so you can see who is thinking, executing, waiting, or already done before switching conversations."

The product page also lists three features designed specifically for Codex:

  • Instant skill triggers: flick the joystick to launch frequently used Codex workflows, such as reviewing a PR (Pull Request), debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Core operations at the press of a key: the command key provides dedicated shortcuts for your most common actions — accept, reject, push-to-talk, open a new chat, and more — reducing context switches and boosting shipping speed.
  • Adjust "brainpower" on the fly: turn the dial to instantly tweak reasoning intensity. Stay fast on simple work, and crank it up the moment you hit a task that needs deeper thought.
